layout_dets.text: The Influence of Silicon on the Pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Corrosion Resistance of an 18Cr-8Ni

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Stainless Steel*

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: B. E. WILDE*

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This paper describes the effect of silicon additions to an 18Cr-8Ni stainless steel (SS) on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance to pit initiation in halide media. Electrochemical polarization measurements con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ducted in aerated 3.5 wt% sodium chloride at 25 C indicate a progressive increase in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: critical breakdown potential (Ec) for 18Cr-8Ni alloys over the range 1.01 to 4.45 wt% silicon (0

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to 17% δ-ferrite), thereby predicting increasing resistance to pit initiation. Pitting corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tests conducted in acidified 10% ferric chloride solution confirmed the trends predicted from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electrochemical studies. Corrosion rates decreasing from 1016 to 50 mdd were observed over

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the silicon range of 1.01 to 4.45 wt%. The latter figure was approximately 20 times better than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that observed on AISI 304 SS.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Analysis of cyclic potentiodynamic anodic polarization curves revealed that although a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: significant increase in pit initiation resistance was observed on the duplex alloys, increasing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: silicon additions (and δ-ferrite content) may increase their susceptibility to crevice corrosion.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Currently available austenitic stainless steels (SSs) have vary-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing resistances to localized corrosion, although they exhibit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: excellent resistance to general corrosive attack. For example,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: AISI 304 SS exhibits excellent general corrosion resistance in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: many applications, but is susceptible to chloride stress corro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sion cracking (SCC), pitting, and intergranular attack (IGA)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: when heat treated to precipitate intergranular chromium car-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bides (sensitized). On the other hand, AISI 316 SS exhibits ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cellent resistance to general and pitting corrosion, but is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: susceptible to chloride SCC and, when sensitized, to IGA. To

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: overcome some of the above limitations and improve the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance of 18Cr-8Ni SSs to localized attack, a program has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been initiated in which silicon additions were made to produce

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloys with duplex microstructures (austenite and ferrite).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Thus far, investigations have indicated that the resistance of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these silicon-stabilized duplex alloys to general acid corro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sion,1 chloride SCC,² and intergranular corrosion (IGC) in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sensitized heat treated condition³ is markedly superior to that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of any currently available commercial austenitic SS.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This paper describes some of the results of this program,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: namely, the resistance of silicon duplex 18Cr-8Ni alloys to pit-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ting corrosion in sodium chloride and acidified ferric chloride

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solutions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: * Submitted for publication May 1985; revised August 1985.

layout_dets.text: Results and Discussion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Potentiodynamic anodic polarization curves for two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloys are shown in Figure 2. A wide range of the potential-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: independent passive current density (CD) was observed on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each alloy, with a clear breakdown potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: marking the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: onset of pit initiation. Previous studies8-10 have shown that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: magnitude of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is qualitatively related to the resistance of an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloy to pit initiation; the more noble or positive the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: value,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the more resistant the material is to pit initiation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The observed breakdown potentials for all of the alloys

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used in this investigation are summarized in Table 2. In the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: experimental duplex alloys (1 through 5), a gradual increase in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was observed as the silicon and δ-ferrite content was in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: creased. On the basis of the data in Table 2, the resistance of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the silicon duplex alloys to pit initiation—with the exception

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of Alloy 1 (1.01 wt% Si)—should be superior to that of AISI 304

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SS used as a control.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Potentiodynamic anodic polarization data11,12 may be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: analyzed to predict alloy resistance to crevice corrosion propa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gation as well as to pit initiation. These analyses show that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: when cyclic potential sweeps are applied to the test specimen,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a marked hysteresis is observed on the polarization plot, as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown in Figure 3. The area in the hysteresis loop is related to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the resistance of the alloy to pit propagation or crevice corro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sion propagation; the larger the area, the more susceptible the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloy is to crevice corrosion. The justification for this latter

layout_dets.text: statement can be seen from the linear relationship shown in

layout_dets.text: Conclusions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The following conclusions may be drawn from the data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: presented:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. The addition of silicon to an 18Cr-8Ni base alloy in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: creased the resistance to pit initiation. The addition of 4.45

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: wt% silicon (17% δ-ferrite) resulted in an alloy with a pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion rate in ferric chloride solution of approximately 2%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of that of AISI 304 SS.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Although silicon duplex SSs exhibit superior resist-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ance to pit initiation, electrochemical data suggest that they

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: may be more susceptible to crevice corrosion.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this report, a new calculation method, which is fundamentally different from those currently

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used, is described for the determination of corrosion parameters from a series of polarization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: points. This method may be applied in any laboratory with a microcomputer, and it requires

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: writing only a short program.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Since the method is not iterative, the calculations may be conducted in a few seconds.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: On the other hand, its advantage over the algebraic methods is that it can accept a large

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: number of points, which affords accuracy to the determinations.
